issues.message: The zero-task shortcut classifies every parsed source without task items as NOFILE. An empty or malformed real tasks.md therefore reaches `unverified:no_declaration_surface` and can be certified by `done`, violating the stated fail-closed behavior. The regression test covers a missing item only when another valid task exists, so this path remains unproven.
issues.fix: Use the declared source kind to return NOFILE only for plan sources; return NOITEM or a parse error for empty/malformed spec sources and add regression coverage.

issues.message: Transcript events are recognized through unrestricted substring searches. The new test explicitly confirms that `cat pytest.ini` counts as a test run; commands that merely echo, grep, or document the init/flip markers can likewise create false work-item boundaries. This makes the reported baseline and Cost ladder measurements inaccurate.
issues.fix: Recognize actual shell command invocations with token-aware boundary matching and add negative tests for cat/grep/echo-only mentions.

issues.message: Checklist trimming operates on individual lines rather than checklist-item blocks: it removes any line containing ✅, retains continuation lines belonging to completed items, and can separate an unfinished item from its nested DoD or notes. Consequently completed content can consume the cap while open-item context is lost, contradicting the whole-unit/unfinished-item guarantee.
issues.fix: Parse top-level checklist bullets with their continuation blocks, retain headers and complete unfinished blocks, and test multiline completed and unfinished items.

issues.message: The suite writes `.mb-config` directly into the checked-in fixture directory and unconditionally deletes it during teardown. Parallel runs can race, and an interrupted or future run can overwrite or remove fixture state outside the test's temporary workspace.
issues.fix: Copy the fixture bank into TMPDIR_T during setup and perform all configuration mutations on that private copy.

issues.message: The new module is 313 lines and exposes more than three public operations spanning JSONL reading, role classification, session aggregation, work-item segmentation, and report assembly. It crosses both SRP thresholds in the review rubric.
issues.fix: Split transcript reading/classification and metric aggregation/segmentation into focused modules while retaining cost_report.py as the small composition API.
